task: CLI child of EPMCDME-16849: emit explicit folder-connection and funding-route signals, enforce folder allowlist/disable, handle /clear, resume and folder-change boundaries with suspension notification, negotiate backend capability, and own the final CLI-to-backend consumer check.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches claude-code-otlp hook/plugin, evidence (stamp/classify/routing/record-store), session pin and project seal, OTLP spool/forwarder, header injection, allowlist/config, plus a new capability-negotiation path and a shared e2e check; new suspension/notification abstraction.

Open design: no explicit folder-to-project signal distinct from project_source, no funding-route field defined, /clear/resume/folder-change behaviour unverified and gated by a spike whose findings reshape the backend contract; suspension UX undesigned. Story lists no open questions, but the spike leaves rework risk.

Privacy-critical, security-sensitive publication gating with no exact precedent (nothing branches on SessionStart clear; no suspension implementation). Closest pattern is the pure classify() fail-closed function and the project pin/seal, which do not cover transition-level disclosure of personal history or duplicate consumption. AC enumerates edge cases (contradictory inputs, per-transition cases) with no existing test template for /clear/resume across personal/work boundaries. Old-backend compatibility adds rollout ordering risk.
Estimated 11-15 modified plus several new files across evidence, otlp-spool, plugin, cli commands, config and tests/integration (including a real-backend e2e).

CLI hook (API/entry), service (evidence/classification), persistence (record store, pin, spool), config/infrastructure (settings, allowlist), and external backend integration with capability negotiation; user notification surface.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk: security/privacy requirement and affects what is published under project permissions
Component Scope: integration with external backend contract and multiple workflows (hook, spool, forwarder)
Borderline 26/27: leaned higher because Technical Risk is XL and Component Scope is XL

split_recommendation.ordering_note: Spike and transition handling first (its findings feed the backend contract), then signals, then capability negotiation and e2e activation after the backend capability ships.

slices.title: Session transition spike and suspension handling
slices.scope: Record session_id, cwd and project across /clear, resume and folder change on an isolated compatible build, report findings to the backend contract, and implement per-transition evaluation with publication suspension and an actionable notification when separation cannot be guaranteed.

slices.title: Explicit-connect and funding-route evidence signals
slices.scope: Emit an explicit folder-connection signal separate from profile-sourced project, add api_based/subscription/unknown funding-route evidence from effective route and authentication, and enforce the folder allowlist and global disable so unconnected folders publish nothing.
slices.depends_on: Session transition spike and suspension handling

slices.title: Capability negotiation and end-to-end consumer check
slices.scope: Negotiate backend capability so an old backend never reports publication as succeeded or freezes a session into an unexpected private destination, and own the real CLI-to-backend e2e check covering AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5, AC8 and AC9/AC11.
